chapter_contribution_notes: Front-facing Walden epigraph/introductory sentence that establishes Thoreau's tone and immediate purpose—an avowed refusal of melancholy and an intent to rouse the reader; minor provenance but useful for tonal continuity.

candidate_blocks.selection_reason: This opening line sets the author's voice and immediate purpose—refusing an ode to dejection and announcing a boastful, rousing intent—so it orients readers to the rhetorical stance of the work and preserves tonal continuity at the book's outset.
candidate_blocks.text:
"I do not propose to write an ode to dejection, but to brag as lustily as
chanticleer in the morning, standing on his roost, if only to wake my neighbors up."
